chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from them (peace be upon him), said:

He was asked about a heap of wheat upon which the fat of the pig had melted. He said: If they are able to wash it, it is eaten, and if they are not able to wash it, it is not eaten. And it was said: Sow it until it sprouts.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wheat contaminated with pig fat if it cannot be washed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *istihlak* (submersion/transformation) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between physical removal of impurity (*najasah*) via washing and biological transformation through germination. It highlights the scholarly debate on whether sowing contaminated grain effectively purifies it by integrating the impurity into the plant's structure, a nuance critical for understanding classical *fiqh* rulings on food purity.
